verdict: CPU stage recorded. Met: t1 (people in the wedge keep their ink exactly, the screen band fails as required), t5 (the orbit is 24% steadier than the base paint), d1 to d5 (no pumping; drift and events never take focus from a speaker or a fight, the lock-off control fails on 916 frames), c1 to c3 (no flash added, no red window, reduced motion stills weave and grain), g2 goldens (GCC and MSVC agree). Missed: t2 (the ink does not fall off out of focus: ratio 1.32 against at most 0.5), t3 (the art scene's E is 0.474 against at least 0.5, and the gaussian control does not fail E on the town, 0.716), t6 (ill-posed: with the camera held the base paint does not change, so its instability is 0 and any rack counts as infinitely worse). GPU parity (g1) and cost (g3) are not yet run.

runs.run1: evidence/tiltshift/cpu-run1.json: the first CPU run (no orbit), MSVC, before addendum B: cMax 8 px at 540 lines; 2 people in the wedge; t2 1.35; t3 town gaussian E 0.88. Kept as recorded.

t2_ink_falls_off.diagnosis: The coarse Kuwahara keeps outlines that lie on region edges (the line sits on the boundary between two flat sectors, so a sector that contains it can still have the least variance). The ink measure is also not robust: Y(no lines) - Y(lines) after two independent Kuwahara runs differs by sector choice. An explicit ink falloff (the paint pass exporting its line layer, attenuated by the CoC) is the likely fix; not built.

t3_painted_not_blurred.diagnosis: By eye the gaussian control is an obvious optical blur and ours is flat paint with hard patch edges (evidence/tiltshift/town-gaussian.png against town-ours.png), but E (a 95th-percentile gradient ratio over all pixels with c >= 4 px) does not separate them on the town: many pixels sit in the mild-defocus range where a gaussian of sigma 1 to 2 px keeps the strong building edges. The metric, not the look, is what fails here; a better one is not substituted after the fact.

t6_temporal_rack.diagnosis: The bound is ill-posed for a held camera: the base paint frame is identical every frame (instability 0.0), so the relative change is unbounded. The tilt-shifted rack's own instability against its optical reference is 0.00245, below a fifth of the base pass's orbit instability (0.0132). Recorded as a miss; the bound is not rewritten.

captures.files: evidence/tiltshift/: town-{plain,band,ours,gaussian,coc}.png, art-{plain,band,ours,gaussian,coc}.png, town-look-{daily,town_map,record,memory,dream,night}.png, crop-band-vs-ours.png (band left, ours right), 960 x 540.
seen: The CoC map follows the world: on the town the in-focus wedge runs along the diagonal street and up the walls where they cross the plane, which a screen band cannot do (t4: 92% of the lens's in-focus pixels are defocused by the matched band).

Town, ours: walls and roofs off the plane flatten into smooth paint with crisp patch edges; the five street people keep their outlines. The screen band smears the people at the street's ends and breaks the lamp post into a jagged line. The gaussian control is a plain optical blur.
Art still life: the defocus is subtle. The paint pass's own large ground blotches survive the coarser Kuwahara, so the model-town read is weak on this scene.

Looks: record shows the halftone dot screen; memory the warm print and vignette. Night shows no visible halation or star: the dusk scene is bright and the lamp globes are a few pixels, so the bright pass's 4 x 4 mean stays near the knee. Dream is hard to tell from daily at this framing. The effects need a darker night scene to be judged.

does_not_prove: That the look is good (the captures are for review). Anything on the GPU: parity and cost are not run yet. Moving figures (the CoC is per frame). The director's timings as a player feels them. The game's browser renderer.
